title: Platform Propulsion: controlplane + routing + auth weekly standup notes
content:
Attendees: Asha, Miguel, Elena, Samir, Priya (SRE)

Context: quick weekly focused standup covering control plane routing/auth/quotas following last week's quota anomaly and this morning's canary which showed an unexpected 25% tail latency bump for ~3 minutes. Goal: capture actions, blockers, and experiment plan for next sprint.

Summary (tl;dr):
- Incident follow-up: root cause likely related to a slow KV read path in the control plane when quota refreshes coincided with routing config rollouts.
- Short-term mitigation: throttle quota refresh job and stagger routing rollout by 2 minutes; implemented via quick config toggle (PR linked).
- Mid-term: add an async quota refresh path + circuit-breaker; spike assigned.
- Auth: rolling token rotation schedule proposed; need QA on legacy mobile token compat.
- Routing: fallback test showed correct behavior but uncovered a race during policy migration. Add explicit migration lock.

Recent metrics / signals:
- Quota refreshes spiked 3x between 01:30-02:00 UTC on 2028-03-06 due to metric ingestion backlog (ingestor incident).
- Control plane p95 latency increased from 85ms to ~110ms for 3 minutes. No customer-facing SLA breach, but internal SLO alert fired.
- Canary (route-propagation v2) exposed a route eval race when quota signals were high.

Incident notes:
- Timeline: 01:26 ingest backlog clears -> 01:29 queued quota-refresh job kicks off -> 01:30 routing rollout starts (auto) -> 01:31 sharp p95 increase observed -> 01:34 job completes, p95 returns to baseline.
- Hypothesis: quota-refresh performs synchronous KV reads for each principal which momentarily blocks the control plane worker responsible for route evaluation. When routing rollout starts same worker becomes contended.
- Evidence: thread dumps show route-eval goroutine blocked on kv.ReadShard; KV telemetry shows elevated read latency during the window.

Short-term actions (today/next 48h):
- M1: Disable auto-routing rollout concurrency with quota refresh toggles (done; PR #3901 merged) — owner: Miguel — due: 2028-03-07 10:00 UTC.
- M2: Reduce quota-refresh concurrency from 50 -> 10 threads and enable jitter — owner: Elena — due: 2028-03-08.
- M3: Add monitoring alert that correlates quota-refresh job concurrency with route-eval latency (dashboard tile + alert runbook) — owner: Priya (SRE) — due: 2028-03-09.

Mid-term work (this sprint):
- Spike: async quota refresh (batched reads + background reconciliation) to avoid blocking critical route-eval paths. Prototype expected by 2028-03-21. — owner: Samir.
- Circuit-breaker: introduce per-worker quota-read circuit to shed load when KV latency climbs. Design doc WIP. — owner: Asha.

Routing notes:
- Migration race: when policy id remapping happens, route-eval sees mixed policy sets for ~10s. Add an explicit migration lock or use versioned snapshots. Prefer snapshots to lock.
- Canary results: functionality OK; performance regressions correlated to quota job spike, not routing logic itself.
- Next test: run canary with quota-refresh disabled and with small synthetic load to validate snapshot approach. — owner: Miguel — due: 2028-03-10.

Auth items:
- Token rotation plan: proposal to shorten refresh token TTL from 30d -> 7d and add a grace-period accept window for older tokens (48h) to reduce churn on control plane. Pros/cons discussed: reduces long-lived credential risk but increases rotation traffic.
- Action: set up compatibility test harness against mobile client (iOS v5.x) and API-gateway to measure extra auth traffic. — owner: Elena — due: 2028-03-14.
- Backchannel: security ops requested we schedule key-rotation rehearsal next month (w/ support and PS). — owner: Asha.

Quotas / Billing signals:
- Observed a small cost bump due to repeated quota re-compute during the backlog; estimate ~$2.4k additional infra cost over 24h. Finance flagged as 'investigate' if similar recurs.
- Optimize: cache per-principal quota for 30s with invalidation on policy change. Tradeoff: slightly stale quotas vs cost. Spike to measure correctness. — owner: Samir.

Open blockers:
- Blocker 1: KV team needs to confirm increased tail latency root cause for that retention window; their action item pending. If KV can't be stabilized, we'll need heavier app-level mitigations.
- Blocker 2: Need agreement on snapshot vs lock for migration approach; rough consensus was snapshot, but need signoff from SRE/Infra.

Decisions made in this meeting:
- Toggle rollouts to avoid concurrency with heavy maintenance jobs (short-term).
- Proceed with async quota-spike prototype this sprint.
- Prefer snapshot-based routing policy migration pending SRE feedback.

Action items (owners + due dates recap):
- Miguel: confirm rollback toggles across regions + run a cross-region canary with quota-refresh disabled — 2028-03-10.
- Elena: throttle quota refresh job, add jitter and document concurrency limits — 2028-03-08.
- Samir: prototype async quota reader (batched KV reads) and cost calc — 2028-03-21.
- Asha: draft circuit-breaker design doc + runbook for shedding quota reads — 2028-03-13.
- Priya (SRE): dashboard + SLO correlation alert — 2028-03-09.
- Security Ops (cc: ops-team): schedule key-rotation rehearsal – propose dates 2028-04-10 or 2028-04-17.

Notes to self (informal):
- Watch for second-order effects when we shorten token TTL; mobile clients can be chatty. Add a conservative rollout with metrics to detect auth error spike.
- Consider a temporary read-cache on the control plane for policies that are read-hot during rollouts. TTL 5s might buy a lot.

Links / references:
- Linear: PLT-1428 (quota-refresh backpressure investigation)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3901 (rollout toggles)
- Slack thread: #platform-controlplane "quota spike postmortem" (link above)

Next meeting: quick sync Tue 2028-03-09 09:30 UTC to confirm mid-term spike progress and to approve circuit-breaker doc for implementation.

End of notes.
